name: ABCmouse / ABCmouse Classic (Age of Learning)
price: Free install, core value gated behind ~$12.99/mo subscription
complaints: FTC action: auto-renewal not clearly disclosed, cancellation deliberately difficult — 'hundreds of thousands of consumers who attempted cancellation nevertheless remained subscribed and billed' (2015-2018); $10M settlement in 2020, refunds mailed 2021
Cancellation only possible via one hard-to-find online link; 100,000+ users tried to cancel via Contact Us and stayed billed
Age of Learning migrated users to a new 'reimagined' app while the 23M-install Classic app decays at ~3.67 stars
Ongoing billing/renewal complaints post-settlement on review platforms
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Khan Academy Kids is free, ad-free, and excellent — but ABCmouse still pulls ~29-33K installs/month on the Classic app alone, proving parents still pay for a structured curriculum path
moatNotes: Massive brand-driven demand ('learning path' curriculum for 2-8). A one-time-purchase or honest-billing full-curriculum app directly attacks the #1 documented pain (billing dark patterns). Content volume is the incumbent moat — narrow wedge (e.g., phonics-to-reading path) advisable

name: Sago Mini World: Kids Games
price: Free install, gated behind Piknik subscription (~$8-10/mo); replaced $2.99-3.99 standalone paid apps that were removed from sale
ratingsCount: Android count not captured; iOS 65K at 4.33 (Android markedly lower)
complaints: Standalone paid Sago Mini apps removed from sale; owners pushed toward the subscription hub
App update dropped standalone-app support inside World — previously purchased games no longer recognized in-app
'Restore purchases' doesn't work; 'I shouldn't have to purchase a subscription since I started buying apps before World was a thing'
Cancelled subscriptions reactivated and charged again the following month; subscription doesn't work across devices as advertised
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: free toddler sandbox competitors are ad-stuffed/IAP-bait; parents explicitly pay for safe ad-free open-ended play — same demand pool as Toca Life (round 1)
moatNotes: Exact Toca pattern replay (Piknik bundles Sago Mini + Toca Boca + Originator). A one-time-purchase toddler sandbox with permanent ownership is the direct counter-position; art/animation quality is the main build cost

name: My PlayHome Plus
price: Free install, paid-gated: areas (school, stores, hospital, houses) sold as IAP; original standalone apps were $3.99 paid purchases
complaints: Owners of the original paid My PlayHome apps report Plus fails to recognize prior ownership — 'rip off to people who already have the my PlayHome apps'
Forced sign-in to access areas already paid for; ownership-detection feature broken in practice
Locked areas visible-but-untouchable to kids, driving purchase pressure complaints
Original paid apps effectively frozen while dev pushes Plus (originals: 350K installs, still $3.99)
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: dollhouse/sandbox genre has free ad-laden clones; the paying audience (parents of 3-6yo) prioritizes ad-free + offline, which free rivals fail
moatNotes: 49M installs at 3.85 is a huge dissatisfied base in a mechanically simple genre (2D dollhouse with physics-lite interactions). Small indie dev (PlayHome Software) — low counter-response capacity. One-time-price 'own it forever' dollhouse is a clean wedge

name: Teach Your Monster to Read
ratingsCount: ~3,000 (Android; iOS is 4.51 from 27K — Android build specifically underperforms)
complaints: Frequent freezes/crashes on Android after specific mini-games (duck game, rocket game); crashes in Practice mode and 10 Minute Adventure acknowledged by dev
App closes on entering birth year (gate screen broken on some devices)
Users report previously purchased versions no longer available to play once new versions went live
Charity-run developer, slow update cadence (last update ~July 2025)
freeIncumbentRisk: High: the same product is free on desktop web (teachyourmonster.org) and Khan Academy Kids covers phonics free — yet 1M+ paid for the mobile-native version, proving willingness to pay for tablet-native phonics
moatNotes: Systematic-synthetic-phonics game with real pedagogy is the moat; the Android build quality gap (3.96 vs 4.51 iOS) is the opening. A technically solid, offline, one-time-purchase phonics adventure wins on execution alone

name: FluentU
price: Free install, gated behind $29.99/mo or $240/yr subscription
complaints: Charged $33/month without clear notification; auto-billing complaints recur across review platforms
Android app bugs: subtitles/translations fail to display in landscape on phones and tablets — core feature broken on mobile
Paying $15-30/mo for a 'small handful of videos' in some languages; flashcards gated behind an additional fee
Consensus even among affiliate reviewers: 'more expensive than the competition' and 'won't be worth the price for most'
freeIncumbentRisk: High: YouTube + Language Reactor / free comprehensible-input channels replicate the core loop for $0; buyer must be sold on curation + integrated SRS convenience
moatNotes: Video-immersion + clickable-subtitle + SRS niche has no well-executed mid-price player; incumbent is priced at ~$240/yr with a 3.49-star app. Content licensing is the real moat/cost — public-domain and creator-partnership content is the workaround

name: Hooked on Phonics Learning
price: Free 7-day trial, then ~$12.99/mo subscription (plus physical 'Practice Pack' upsell)
complaints: BBB: 50+ complaints in 3 years citing incorrect billing amounts and difficult cancellation
Trustpilot: charged even after cancelling; charged immediately after trial ends
Cannot cancel from inside the app; subscription + separate Practice Pack billing confuses parents
No refunds for forgotten renewals
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Khan Academy Kids and free phonics content; but 35-year brand keeps pulling paying parents into a resented billing model — demand signal, not a direct clone economics signal
moatNotes: Weakest of the six on verified numbers (rating hovers right at the 4.1 cutoff, ratings count unverified). Treat as secondary validation of the 'parents pay for structured learn-to-read' thesis behind ABCmouse/Teach Your Monster rather than a primary target

_note: Investigated but rejected (failed rubric): Rosetta Stone (Trustpilot anger real but Play apps rate 4.6-4.76), Memrise/Pimsleur/LingQ/HiNative/Drops/Beelinguapp/LingoDeer/Innovative Language (all 4.2+ on Play), Endless Alphabet (license-loss complaints but 4.46), LetterSchool (paid-to-sub betrayal real but 4.25), Reading Eggs (4.48), Stack the States (healthy), Montessorium (no Android abandonment evidence), Dr. Panda (actively updated).
